key_insight: DFT predicts that lead-free double perovskites K/Rb2SnGeX6 are stable, ductile, and highly tunable, with bandgaps spanning 1.44 to 0.64 eV and strong thermoelectric performance.
engineering_relevance: This makes the family promising for safer photovoltaic absorbers, tandem/near-IR optoelectronics, and high-ZT waste-heat recovery materials.
method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) across K/Rb and Cl/Br/I compositions
Structural stability screened using formation energies, tolerance factors, and octahedral factors
Mechanical, electronic, optical, and thermoelectric properties analyzed from calculated elastic, band, and transport descriptors
evidence_signal: The abstract reports all six compounds are thermodynamically stable and cubic, with direct bandgaps and a peak thermoelectric figure of merit of ZT = 2.4 for K2SnGeI6 at 1000 K.
watch_item: These are computational predictions, so experimental synthesis quality, defect tolerance, and real-device performance still need validation.
paper_title: First-Principles Study of Novel Lead-Free Double Perovskite \b{eta}2SnGeX6 (\b{eta} = K, Rb; X = Cl, Br, I) for thermomechanical, optoelectronic and outstanding thermoelectric applications
